title: Transactions: purchase, redemption, cut-offs, SIP, STP and SWP
objectives: Apply cut-off rules to decide which NAV applies.
body_md:
## Cut-off times (key rules)

| Transaction | Cut-off | NAV applied |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase in equity and most debt schemes | 3:00 pm | Same-day NAV if funds are available; else next business day |
| Purchase in **liquid / overnight** schemes | 1:30 pm | Based on funds available for utilisation |
| Redemption (all) | 3:00 pm | Same-day NAV |
| After cut-off | | Next business day's NAV |

Redemption proceeds are paid within **3 working days** (faster for liquid funds).

## Systematic plans

- **SIP:** invest a fixed amount at regular intervals; gives **rupee cost averaging**.
- **STP:** transfer a fixed amount from one scheme to another within the same AMC, often from debt to equity.
- **SWP:** withdraw a fixed amount at intervals from a lump sum; useful for retirement income.

## Switching

A **switch** moves money between schemes (or plans) of the same AMC. It is treated as a redemption plus a purchase, so **tax and exit load** may apply.

> **Exam tip:** Remember 3:00 pm for most, 1:30 pm for liquid and overnight purchase.
example: An investor places a purchase of an equity fund at 3:20 pm with funds credited. The applicable NAV is the next business day's.
say: Applications after 3 pm get the next day's NAV.
A switch is a redemption and a purchase, so tax can apply.
never: You will always get today's NAV whenever you invest.
